A 16-bit SNES-style PIXEL ART character WALK sheet on a SOLID FLAT PURE WHITE background (#FFFFFF, completely uniform). Layout: 3 ROWS by 3 COLUMNS of sprites, evenly spaced, with a wide empty white margin on all four sides and a clear white gap between every sprite — nothing may touch, overlap or be cut off by any edge, especially the bottom row. Every sprite is the SAME character at the SAME size and the SAME pixel scale. THE CHARACTER, drawn identically in all nine frames: {CHARACTER}. THE THREE COLUMNS are the walk cycle, left to right: Column 1 = MID-STEP. In the SIDE row this means her LEFT foot planted forward and her right foot back with a clear gap between them. In the FRONT and BACK rows a forward foot is invisible from that angle, so instead her LEFT leg is LIFTED — knee bent, that foot clearly raised off the ground, the right leg straight and planted. Arms swinging. Column 2 = NEUTRAL STANDING — both legs straight and together directly under the body, arms hanging relaxed, no stride, no lean, no leaning weapon pose. This is the standing-still pose and it must be obviously different from columns 1 and 3. Column 3 = MID-STEP with the legs swapped: in the SIDE row her RIGHT foot is planted forward and her left foot back; in the FRONT and BACK rows her RIGHT leg is LIFTED with the knee bent and the foot raised, the left leg straight and planted. It is the opposite stride to column 1 and clearly NOT a repeat of the standing pose in column 2. THE THREE ROWS are directions, and the direction must hold across ALL THREE frames of its row without exception — including the neutral standing frame: Row 1 = seen from the FRONT, facing the viewer, with her shoulders and hips SQUARE to the camera in all three frames — both sides of her body equally visible, both ears visible, face pointing straight at the viewer. Do NOT rotate her body into a side or three-quarter pose to show the step; the step is shown by the lifted knee alone. Row 2 = strict SIDE PROFILE FACING RIGHT — head in profile, nose pointing right, one shoulder to the viewer, in all three frames INCLUDING the neutral standing one; never turned to face the viewer. Row 3 = seen from BEHIND — the back of the head and body, NO face, NO eyes, NO snout — with her shoulders and hips SQUARE to the camera in all three frames, both sides equally visible. Do NOT rotate her into a side or three-quarter pose to show the step; the step is shown by the lifted knee alone. ART STYLE: chunky flat cartoon pixel art, big simple shapes, flat solid colours, a thick black outline, no anti-aliasing, no gradients, no dithering, no texture inside a colour block. Nothing else in the image: no grid lines, no boxes, no frames, no labels, no text, no numbers, no shadows, and NO GROUND LINE — no floor bar, platform, plinth, baseline stripe or patch of ground drawn under the feet. The character floats on empty background; the game draws its own floor.
